lastCommit.message:
OTA-1847 — the process says where it was

A Sentry classification audit of the native-death signature that
correlates with `aliveStage: 'qwen:deferred'`. Two defects, neither of
them Qwen.

D1 — LIFECYCLE OWNERSHIP. `clearLiveBreadcrumb()`, the orderly-exit latch
that tells a clean background transition from a death, was owned by
`startRuntimePressureWatch`, which is started at the END of `bootQwen` —
and since OTA-1493 `bootQwen` waits for the FIRST PLAYER ACTION. On the
title screen, on character creation, and through every life backgrounded
before the first tap, nobody owned the latch at all: the crumb survived,
hydrate() promoted it, and "player put the phone down and the OS took the
process" was filed as a high-severity native death. That is also why the
signature correlates with the deferred Qwen stage without Qwen being
causal — `qwen:deferred` is simply what the stage field says while Qwen
is waiting.

Ownership moves to the alive beat, which App.tsx starts at the app root,
unconditionally, on every platform, from the first frame. The latch is
still the LAST statement of the background branch: OTA-1377 chose that
position and OTA-1413 kept it, and reaching it is itself the proof the
transition completed. Only the owner changed, not the rule. The pressure
watch keeps every instrument it had and gives up the latch entirely.

D2 — SEVERITY AND GROUPING. The classifier was already right
(`isFatal: false`); the severity was invented downstream by a two-rung
ternary in the transport, and the fingerprint grouped on `stage`, which
for a background disappearance is whatever happened to be written last —
splintering one indistinguishable event across a dozen issues.

The boot slice now classifies on `crumb.appState`, which the beat already
persists synchronously and which the classifier previously spent on
prose, plus one optional bounded boolean (`inGame`, read from the store's
own `activeSlotId != null && player != null` at beat time, absent-safe).
It emits a bounded `impact`:

  background-idle   -> info    -> [kind, 'background-idle']
  background-active -> warning -> [kind, 'background-active']

Foreground deaths, legacy crumbs with no appState, and clean exits are
untouched: same level, same fingerprint, same record or no record.

THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: a previous process that
disappeared while backgrounded cannot be retrospectively identified as OS
reclaim, force-stop, reboot, update, developer kill, or another unclean
disappearance from the available Tartaria evidence. This stops claiming
to know which one it was; it does not start claiming to know.

Tests: new suite ota1847TheProcessSaysWhereItWas (38) drives the real
hydrate() over staged survivors. Five pinned suites follow the code
honestly — ota1377 (x3, the latch's new owner, and the old owner proven
to have let go), ota1401 (the two-arm fingerprint, plus a new direct
assertion that it is never built from the message), ota1413 (x3),
ota1567, ota1741.

Two guards were converted rather than loosened, both strictly stronger:
the `isFatal` pin in ota1567/ota1741 becomes a whitespace-tolerant shape
(check:quotedpins stays at its 112 baseline, not raised), and ota1177's
character-distance window — already raised once by an unrelated OTA —
becomes the claim it stood for: the three sinks arm in order with no
`await` anywhere between the first and the last.

Fast surface 1341/1341 suites, 15,105 passed. 25/25 local gates.
